_comment: Editorial half of the project manifest. The mechanical half — main_version,
latest_release, supported TYPO3 and PHP versions — is derived by
landingpage/render.mjs from ext_emconf.php and composer.json and must not be
The build publishes the merged result at <site>/project-manifest.json, which
stage is 'alpha' and every page states it above the fold. Changing it here
changes it everywhere — which is the point, and the reason it is not written
providers: Whatever nr-llm is configured with — this extension has no provider of its own.

capabilities.label: A chat assistant inside the TYPO3 backend
capabilities.detail: Editors ask in the backend they already work in; no separate tool and no separate login.

capabilities.label: Tools available in chat
capabilities.detail: Chat uses enabled built-in tools within the user’s permissions. Tools imported from remote MCP servers are disabled by default and require an administrator account even after activation.

capabilities.label: Conversation history per backend user
capabilities.detail: A run can be re-read afterwards, which is what makes a review possible at all.

capabilities.label: Approval for built-in writing tools
capabilities.detail: Built-in writing tools require approval. For remote MCP tools, the server setting determines whether chat asks before a call.

security_controls.label: Provider, budget and permission controls come from nr-llm
security_controls.detail: This extension adds an interface; it does not add a second key store, a second budget or a second permission model.

security_controls.label: Read-only by default
security_controls.detail: Built-in writing tools are disabled by default. An administrator must enable them before use.

security_controls.label: Run history and approval decisions
security_controls.detail: With the default metadata policy, saved tool events in the nr-llm run omit argument values. The pending approval preview can still display those values.

security_controls.label: Backend-group permissions apply
security_controls.detail: The agent cannot reach what the acting user cannot reach; TYPO3's own access rules are not bypassed.

cost_controls.label: Budgets and analytics from nr-llm
cost_controls.detail: Per-user request, token and cost limits apply to agent runs like any other AI use on the site.

ai.intended_purpose: A controlled assistant in the TYPO3 backend: finding and summarising content an editor may already see, preparing changes, and executing a released change after an explicit human approval.
excluded_uses: Unattended operation. Alpha means evaluate it with someone watching.
Replacing an editor's judgement. It drafts; a person decides.
Bypassing TYPO3 permissions. It cannot reach what the acting user cannot reach.
Anything with a legal, financial or personnel consequence.
models: Whatever nr-llm is configured with. This extension chooses no provider and holds no key.
data: The editor's question, the conversation history of that run, and whatever a released tool returns.
The tools receive the arguments needed for the proposed action.

Image analysis is enabled by default. For alt text suggestions, the model receives a scaled copy. Chat can send the attached image itself and, for models that support it, the full PDF. Context-only mode can still send extracted PDF text.
ai.human_oversight: Built-in writing tools require approval. For remote MCP tools, the server setting determines whether chat asks before a call. One decision covers the pending calls in a round.
ai.permissions: Chat uses enabled built-in tools within the user’s permissions. Tools imported from remote MCP servers are disabled by default and require an administrator account even after activation.
ai.logging: With the default metadata policy, saved tool events in the nr-llm run omit argument values. The pending approval preview can still display those values.
ai.retention: Conversations and audit records live in the site's database and follow the site's own retention rules.
ai.cost_control: Inherited from nr-llm: per-user budgets on requests, tokens or estimated cost.
security_controls: Read-only by default; writing tools ship disabled
Approval gate with a recorded decision
TYPO3 backend permissions enforced, not bypassed
Provider keys and budgets stay in nr-llm
known_limitations: Alpha. Interfaces, tool contracts and configuration can still change between releases.
Prompt injection through content the agent reads is possible. The tool release list and the approval gate are the mitigation, not immunity.
The model can misread an instruction and propose the wrong change. That is what the approval is for — an approver who does not read the proposal removes the control.
Excessive agency is a design risk of any agent. Release the smallest useful tool set, not the largest available one.
It is only as reliable as the model behind it, and that model is configured elsewhere.
